verdict.rationale: Docusaurus documents built-in i18n support. Localization comes out of the box, with docs translated via git or Crowdin and deployed per locale, and right-to-left locales are supported. This covers publishing translated content in multiple languages. The evidence does not explicitly cover translating navigation elements such as the sidebar, navbar or locale switcher, so coverage is partial. missing for 10: explicit evidence of translated navigation (sidebar/navbar labels, locale dropdown), independent or hands-on corroboration of the i18n workflow

support.subject: As a technical writer, I publish my docs in multiple languages with translated navigation and content

citations.quote: It is easy to translate a Docusaurus website with its internationalization (i18n) support.
Localization comes out-of-the-box. Use git, Crowdin, or any other translation manager to translate your docs and deploy them individually.
**RTL support**: locales reading right-to-left (Arabic, Hebrew, etc.) are supported and easy to implement
